October 13, 2026

Medicaid work requirements take effect January 1

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Beginning January 1, Medicaid recipients in the 44 states that expanded the program will have to prove they are working, attending school, or volunteering at least 80 hours a month, or earning at least $580 a month, and will have to re-certify every six months instead of annually. Retroactive coverage will be narrowed from three months to as little as one or two months in some states, and some legal immigrants will become ineligible. Accounting mechanisms that benefit children's hospitals are also expected to be cut. People who lose work and then regain it may still be denied coverage where states require three months of work before eligibility.

Protester in Epstein files shirt assaulted at Ohio Trump rally

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

A protester wearing a shirt reading "release the Epstein files" was punched repeatedly by attendees at a Trump campaign rally in Columbus, Ohio on October 12, with the crowd chanting "USA" during the incident. Police eventually removed the protester from the venue; none of the attendees involved were escorted out or charged. From the stage, the president commented on the protester's weight rather than condemning the violence. Footage of the incident was recorded by TMZ and has been restricted on some platforms.

Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in immigration records investigation

tags: politics, legal, immigration
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Homeland Security Investigations agents executed a court-authorized search warrant at the Washington-area home of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota before dawn on Monday. A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed the search is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation, which reporting indicates concerns potential fraud in immigration documents completed by Omar's late father when she was a child. Omar has not been charged with a crime.

Federal judge halts taxpayer-funded TV ads featuring Trump

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A federal judge has temporarily ordered the administration to stop running taxpayer-funded television advertisements featuring the president. The Department of Homeland Security had awarded a $20 million contract for the campaign ahead of the midterm elections. Trump defended the ads but later said political funds could cover them, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune also criticized the use of taxpayer money. The order lasts two weeks.

US bankruptcy filings up 11 percent as inflation and debt squeeze households

tags: economy, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Figures from the American Bankruptcy Institute show an 11 percent year-over-year increase in bankruptcy filings for the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025. More than 469,000 individual and commercial filings have been recorded so far this year. The increase is attributed to high interest rates, persistent inflation, and rising costs for households and small businesses.

Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy truce that Kyiv and Moscow have not confirmed

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an immediate ceasefire on strikes against energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy said Ukraine learned of the announcement from the media, and Russia has not confirmed any agreement. Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities continued after the announcement. Ukraine says it will halt strikes on Russian energy sites if Moscow does the same.

New White House press secretary's first briefing draws scrutiny over credentials

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia delivered her first briefing, which lasted about 14 minutes and consisted largely of an eight-minute prepared monologue followed by two or three questions before she abruptly ended it. She said Kimberly Guilfoyle, the ambassador to Greece who is under investigation there over an alleged pay-to-play scheme, had been asked to resign. Asked where she passed the bar exam, Zacharia referred to practising in China; there is no evidence she passed a bar exam in any US state, and the answer drew criticism from some on the right.

US measles cases top 4,000, a 35-year high

tags: health
sources: @groundnews

CDC data confirmed Friday shows 4,080 measles cases across 47 states and Washington, DC this year, the highest total in 35 years. Pennsylvania accounts for 1,105 of them, more than any other state and over 400 ahead of South Carolina. Children aged 5 to 19 make up 42 percent of cases, children under 5 account for 17 percent, and adults 40 percent. Pennsylvania's outbreak is centred in Lancaster County among Plain communities where vaccination rates fall below the state average; health officials say two MMR doses are 97 percent effective.

Utah's unelected development boards capture taxes and clear the way for data centers

tags: politics, tech, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

Three Utah boards whose members are appointed rather than elected — the Military Installation Development Authority, the Utah Inland Port Authority, and the state trust lands agency SITLA — control billions in land, taxes, and development. MIDA and UIPA can retain 75 percent of new property taxes in their zones for 25 years, extendable by 15 more, and can issue bonds against those revenues; MIDA has created a special taxing district containing zero registered voters and approved the Stratos data center campus in Box Elder County without environmental or traffic studies. SITLA's board voted unanimously last month to lease a square mile of trust land to an experimental nuclear startup for up to 100 years. A 2024 law lets developers convert projects into their own cities to bypass counties, and a 2026 law lets the state move lawsuits against it to a new three-judge panel; lawmakers who expanded these powers are on the November 3 ballot.

Campaign presses administration to restore Grand Staircase-Escalante and Bears Ears

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A letter-writing campaign is calling on the administration to restore the Grand Staircase-Escalante and Bears Ears national monuments, more than 90 percent of which has been removed from protected status by proclamation that described the land as not special enough to protect. Organizers cite polling showing 91 percent of Western voters want national monuments left intact and two-thirds of Utahns support protection, and say residents were not consulted. Five handwritten letters are being delivered to the administration directly.

State Department names anti-trafficking ambassador as Epstein files remain sealed

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration announced that Barbara Thornell has joined as ambassador-at-large to monitor and combat trafficking in persons, in an announcement made by Assistant Secretary Riley Barnes. Thornell's remit is to target transnational crime exploiting men, women, and children for profit. The appointment drew immediate calls for attention to unindicted Jeffrey Epstein co-conspirators, as the Department of Justice continues to withhold millions of pages of Epstein files.

Ken Paxton reported celebrating in Dubai alongside fugitives

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Wall Street Journal reported that Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for Senate in Texas, spent New Year in Dubai with his girlfriend and a fugitive named Samir Suhail. The individuals are accused of healthcare fraud, and one donated more than $100,000 to Paxton's campaign. Paxton was serving as Texas attorney general, the state's top law enforcement officer, at the time.

Grassley files for reelection at 93

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa has officially filed for reelection in 2028. He is currently 93 and would be 101 at the end of the term in 2035. Grassley was first elected to the House of Representatives in 1974 and to the Senate in 1980.

Air Force major held in solitary confinement after calling for Trump's impeachment

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Air Force Maj. Jason Watson, who called for the president's impeachment while in uniform at the Capitol, has remained in solitary confinement for nearly two months, according to his attorney. Watson faces military charges and has not been convicted. His attorney says he is isolated even during meals and exercise; a hearing officer cited restrictions on housing him with civilian detainees.

Trump ad promises $5,000 payments to adult citizens if Republicans win

tags: politics, economy
sources: @ericmoutsos

A 33-second advertisement posted by the president promises every adult citizen in the United States $5,000 and says Democratic policies would instead raise taxes and bring an economic depression. The ad frames the midterm outcome as a choice between economic success and collapse. No mechanism for the payments was described.

Trump's Ohio rally remarks draw questions about his fitness

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

At a rally in Ohio, the president delivered extended remarks praising a senator's physique, saying he had examined the man's body, hands, and jawline because he had not known he was an athlete. He also disputed global warming by asserting that ice is larger than it has been before, and made remarks about transgender people. Reporters in the building described repeated disjointed passages, and some supporters left before the event ended.

Navy plans costly carrier catapult redesign on advice of unlocatable sailor

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump said a veteran sailor named "Bill Jones" helped persuade him to return Navy aircraft carriers to steam catapults. Pentagon officials reportedly searched for the sailor and could not find him. The Navy is nonetheless planning a redesign that experts say could cost billions of dollars.

Hackers heat refrigerators at hundreds of French supermarkets

tags: tech, legal
sources: @groundnews

Hackers raised refrigerator temperatures to 122°F at hundreds of French supermarkets overnight, causing fires and widespread food losses. Les Mousquetaires reported 150 affected Intermarché stores where refrigerators stayed heated for six hours, Carrefour reported 80 affected stores, and Cooperative U confirmed it was also targeted. French prosecutors called the attack large-scale, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu ordered an investigation, and France is coordinating with European authorities over possible attacks abroad. Danish refrigeration supplier Danfoss said the affected systems ran outdated firmware.

No Kings rally set for Utah State Capitol on October 17

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A No Kings rally will be held on the steps of the Utah State Capitol in Salt Lake City on Saturday, October 17 from 3 to 5 pm. Organizers are urging attendees to bring signs and keep the event peaceful. The event is being promoted alongside voting messaging as Utah ballots go out around October 14.

Cornell bans fraternity parties and brings in state police for misconduct cases

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Cornell University has banned parties and social gatherings at fraternity houses through the end of the 2026-27 academic year after criticism of its handling of an alleged sexual assault at a fraternity house in 2024. President Michael Kotlikoff announced a zero-tolerance policy under which chapters that violate the rules face immediate emergency suspension, and the university will review whether fraternity life can continue. New York State Police investigators will take over sexual misconduct cases from campus police, and the university will hire a case manager to assist students who report misconduct.

Palantir CTO says some AI researchers have taken up smoking on the bet AI will cure cancer

tags: tech, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Palantir's chief technology officer said in the past day that some AI researchers have started smoking cigarettes as a demonstration of confidence that AI will cure cancer. The stated logic is that the researchers are signalling total belief in the technology's capabilities. AI has not cured lung cancer.
